name: Question 7
worked_solution:
The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+3$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{2}+5x-9}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+4)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{C}{x+4}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $({x}^{2}+3)(x+4),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+5x-9 & =(Ax+B)(x+4)+C({x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=2,B=-3,$ and $C=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{2}+5x-9}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+4)} & =\frac{2x-3}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{1}{x+4}\end{aligned}
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+5x-9}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x-3}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{1}{x+4})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x-3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+4}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+3.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+3| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x & =3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}x}{3}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+4}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+4|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+5x-9}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x-3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3)-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}x}{3})+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+4|+K\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate ∫3x2+5x−9(x2+3)(x+4)dx.

a
 2ln⁡(x2+3)−3arctan⁡(3x3)+K
b
 ln⁡(x2+3)−3arctan⁡(3x3)+ln⁡|x+4|+K
c
 2ln⁡(x2+3)−33arctan⁡(3x3)+ln⁡|x+4|+K
d
 −ln⁡(x2+3)+3arctan⁡(3x3)+3ln⁡|x+4|+K
e

EXPLANATION

The quadratic factor x2+3 is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition: 3x2+5x−9(x2+3)(x+4)=Ax+Bx2+3+Cx+4

To determine the coefficients A,B, and C, we first multiply both sides of the above equation by (x2+3)(x+4), and we get 3x2+5x−9=(Ax+B)(x+4)+C(x2+3).

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get A=2,B=−3, and C=1. Therefore, 3x2+5x−9(x2+3)(x+4)=2x−3x2+3+1x+4

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end. ∫3x2+5x−9(x2+3)(x+4)dx=∫(2x−3x2+3+1x+4)dx=∫2xx2+3dx−3∫1x2+3dx+∫1x+4dx

For the first integral, we use the substitution u=x2+3. Then du=2xdx, and we get ∫2xx2+3dx=∫1udu=ln⁡|u|=ln⁡|x2+3|=ln⁡(x2+3).

For the second integral, we use the fact that ∫1x2+a2dx=1aarctan⁡(xa), which results in 3∫1x2+3dx=3⋅13⋅arctan⁡(x3)=3arctan⁡(3x3).

Finally, for the third integral, we have ∫1x+4dx=ln⁡|x+4|.

So, we get the following result: ∫3x2+5x−9(x2+3)(x+4)dx=∫2xx2+3dx−3∫1x2+3dx+∫1x+4dx=ln⁡(x2+3)−3arctan⁡(3x3)+ln⁡|x+4|+K
